text.p: Montenegro's President Momir Bulatovic has warned opposition leaders that they face possible legal action for allegations of rampant corruption in the ruling party, Yugoslav news media reported on Thursday.
"I do not know whether the opposition considers that we individually...stole some money," Bulatovic was quoted as saying by a Montenegrin news agency.
"If they do, then that can be established through court proceedings which we will, after the elections, absolutely insist on," said Bulatovic, quoted by Montena-Faks.

In the campaign for federal and local elections in rump Yugoslavia, opposition parties have alleged Montenegro's ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) have used their positions to steal from state coffers and profit from smuggling.
The DPS is allied with Serbia's ruling Socialist party dominated by Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
Serbia and tiny Montenegro make up rump Yugoslavia.
Bulatovic said he, Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic and parliament speaker Svetozar Marovic were fed up with what he called false accusations from opposition parties.

"Independently of the posts we are in, we have the right, under mechanisms of democratic institutions -- this is not a threat of any kind, it is just protection of moral integrity of our personalities -- to establish whether these accusations have any grounds," he was quoted as saying.
The "National Unity" opposition coalition drew thousands of people to a campaign rally on Wednesday in the Montenegrin capital Podgorica, local news media reported.
